messages:
andrew: quick update — ran a few benchmark passes to investigate the hit-rate divergence we saw yesterday (replay vs synthetic). Mixed short-prefix load looks like the trigger.

maya: can you paste the exact commands and configs you used? which kernels and batcher settings?

andrew: yep, ran these locally: 
```
./replay_harness --trace=prod_prefixes_2026-03-10.json --qps=1200 --clients=48 \
  --kvcache-shards=16 --cache-size=2GB --batcher=dynamic --runtime-kernel=auto
```
and also a synthetic Poisson run: 
```
./synthetic_driver --pattern=poisson --qps=1200 --clients=48 --seq-dist=short-heavy
```

sam: note that `auto` lets the runtime pick fused_attn on newer GPUs which alters batch assembly. please try pinned kernels (cuda_mm, fused_attn variants) to isolate.

andrew: did that. Pinned three modes: auto, cuda_mm, fused_int8_fused_attn. Short-prefix mixed workload (qps=1200) numbers:
- auto: hit-rate 68%, p50 token-lat 4.1ms, p95 token-lat 18.6ms
- cuda_mm: hit-rate 69%, p50 4.4ms, p95 21.2ms
- fused_int8_fused_attn: hit-rate 66%, p50 3.2ms, p95 25.9ms

maya: interesting — fused gives better p50 but worse p95 and lower hit-rate. hypothesis: batching heuristic favors bigger batches which changes insertion order into KV, increasing evictions for short prefixes.

kai: I think the batcher flush timing interacts badly with KV warmup. If the batcher waits longer to coalesce, cold prefixes are inserted later and evict older entries across shards. Short prefixes amplify churn.

olivia: profiler traces show eviction thrash: high insert spikes when many short sequences arrive and the global LRU oscillates across shards. I captured a couple flamegraph snapshots.

perf-bot: perf-ci: regression detected in main -> 1746de3 (p95 tokens +12% on kvcache scenario)

infra-bot: deploy note: can reproduce on dedicated-staging with same config (shards=16, cache=2GB)

andrew: proposed repro plan: 
1) apples-to-apples: freeze kernel, freeze batcher strategy, deterministicize client ordering (seed), run replay vs synthetic with same request order.
2) batching litmus: synthetic sweep over short/long prefix ratio (0->100% in 10% steps) to map hit-rate/latency surface.
3) eviction stress: synthetic bursty inserts while reading long-lived prefixes; measure eviction rate, thrash (evictions/sec), and staleness events.

sam: for apples-to-apples also freeze placement and shard mapping. use `--random-seed` in harness to make client interleavings deterministic.

kai: patch idea for batcher: bias flush timer when insert_rate > HOT_INSERT_THRESH to avoid waiting for large batches that reorder inserts. Pseudocode: 
```
if batch.size >= max_batch or batch.latency_est >= target_p95:
    flush(batch)
elif insert_rate > HOT_INSERT_THRESH and batch.wait_time > SHORT_WAIT_THRESH:
    flush(batch)
```

olivia: for eviction mitigation: move to per-shard async eviction and an approximate LRU window to avoid global oscillation. add per-key generation counters so stale writes don't overwrite newer entries.

henry: we also need a concurrency correctness litmus — saw a single incorrect KV read under high concurrency. Proposed property test: generate N operations across M shards with randomized interleavings, assert that a kv_get after a kv_insert returns the inserted value or defined fallback, and detect any read-before-write anomalies.

andrew: agreed. I'll open PRs: batching heuristic tweak + unit/perf tests, per-shard eviction prototype, and deterministic apples-to-apples harness configs + run IDs.

maya: small request: tag runs with metadata (kernel, batcher, seed, qps, seq-dist) so the perf dashboard can ingest them automatically.

andrew: will do. initial apples-to-apples run IDs on staging: run-20260317-001 (cuda_mm), run-20260317-002 (fused_int8_fused_attn). I'll upload traces + perf summaries to the artifacts bucket.

olivia: once traces available I can use `kv-warmup-visualizer` to plot insertion order vs eviction timeline and highlight thrash windows. :eyes:

henry: +1 to add the concurrency property test to perf-ci as a quick smoke job (cheap config, 30s) so regressions show up early.

sam: also add a kernel microbench (very lightweight) to capture per-token kernel variance — that helps explain p95 differences between kernels.

andrew: timeline: today — apples-to-apples runs and trace upload. tomorrow — batching PR draft. EOD Thurs — eviction prototype branch. ping me for staging access.

maya: thanks, this plan sounds good. :thumbsup:

andrew: assigning tasks to myself; will open PRs and post links here when ready.
